newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares slump in ho-hum trade.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares slump in ho-hum trade.

text.p: Chilean blue chips slipped in listless afternoon trading, following Wall Street's lead and finding little local news to animate the market.
The selective IPSA index closed off 0.57 percent at 90.33 points. The all-share IGPA dipped 0.6 percent to 4963.75 points on moderate volume of 13.7 billion pesos.
Brokers said they saw little chance of a long-expected Christmas rally and doubted the IPSA would end the year any higher than 93 or 95 points, barring some major change in the market's climate.
"Maybe it will pick up a little, but there is nothing in this situation to suggest a recovery between now and the end of the year," said one broker.
Endesa slipped two percent to 220.5 pesos, tracking its American Depositary Receipt decline, despite a flurry of expansion news.

Endesa said that its Peruvian unit Edegel inaugurated a new power generator; that it would start studies on building a copper refinery with Finland's Outokumpu; and announced it was in early talks with Canada's Noranda to build a long-delayed aluminum smelter.

Cervecerias Unidas was the day's leading decliner, falling 9.3 percent on very light volume to 1,360 pesos on rumors that a coming ADR issue would be priced considerably below market expectations, brokers said.
Other decliners included steelmaker CAP, off 2.6 percent to 915 pesos, and Telex-Chile, off 1.8 percent to 1100 pesos, after a sell recommendation from Santander Investment.
Gainers included newly-placed Almacenes Paris, up 1.1 percent to 349 pesos on strong volume, and Inforsa, up 1.5 percent to 67 pesos.
